construct: THE FOCUS-RING RESERVATION IDIOM under a state that changes only the WIDTH: the rest plane is `outline: 2px solid transparent` (a real, drawn `outline-style: solid` over a fully transparent colour) and `:focus-visible` sets `outline-width: 4px`
why: THE ANTI-LOOSENING GUARD for focus-ring-declared-style-only. Reading the state's outline through the CSS cascade — the override first, the resting fact behind it — is what lets the keyword-only ring lower, and the SAME reading would complete the pair here, where the resting colour is `transparent` and CSS paints nothing at any width. That is exactly what Carbon spells on Accordion's icon, Tabs' nav item and TextInput (all three resolve to #00000000, measured), and drawing it would put a canvas ring around parts the library leaves bare — the HARMFUL class. The colour must still have to PAINT, which is the same value test the base plane's `outlineColorPaints` already applies; the cascade widens where the fact comes from, never whether it inks.
expectWhere: anatomy.root.states.focus-visible.outline-width (the CSS half carries the width faithfully; the refusal this case guards is the CANVAS half)

canvas.note: nothing may draw: a stroke here is a ring around a component the library renders with none, at every width
